fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. After they deliberated among themselves, the text says they answered, “We do not know.” Think about that for a second. They huddled up, and the final answer was four words long. I've burned a whole batch with less effort than that.

That's the question exactly, baker. The chief priests and elders come up to Him in the temple courts and ask, “By what authority are You doing these things?” Then they add, “And who gave You this authority?” They want to know where His authority for doing these things comes from.

Close in spirit, friend, because it's about where His authority comes from. But the text has them ask something different: “And who gave You this authority?” That's about who gave Him the authority to do these things, not who gave Him lessons. The leaders never ask about His teachers in this passage.

Jerusalem isn't in the question, friend. Jesus asks, “What was the source of John’s baptism? Was it from heaven or from men?” He's asking where the baptism came from, and the choices are heaven or men. No maps needed.

The Romans never show up in this passage, friend. The leaders say, “we are afraid of the people, for they all regard John as a prophet.” Their worry is the people, not the Romans. Sometimes the people around you are more nerve-racking than any empire.

Nobody suggests asking the people, friend. The leaders are afraid of the people, but their actual answer is, “We do not know.” They hand the question back with no answer at all. Then Jesus replies to them.
Ask John himself? Nice idea, friend, but nobody says it. The leaders only say, “We do not know.” They don't point Jesus to anybody. Not even a "let me get back to you."
No servants in this story, friend. The first son says no, but then he “…changed his mind and went.” The story has him going. It doesn't have him sending anybody.
Right, baker. The second son said, “I will, sir…” but the text goes on, “But he did not go.” A nice yes with no vineyard behind it. That's the sting in the story.

Before is the word, baker. Jesus says, “Truly I tell you, the tax collectors and prostitutes are entering the kingdom of God before you.” That's a sharp thing to say to the chief priests and elders. The tax collectors and prostitutes are going in ahead of them.

That's right, baker. Jesus says, “And even after you saw this, you did not repent and believe him.” They saw the tax collectors and prostitutes believe John, and they still didn't repent. That's the second son's story all over again.
